proposal.name: Request-local tree speculation with scalar verification
proposal.idea: Allocate the existing linear draft’s verification budget to a tree of likely continuations using the current successor counts. Verify each distinct node once through projection-major singleton operations, then follow exact target argmax predictions through the tree and retain only that path’s KV state.
proposal.cost_removed: With B draft nodes and a accepted tokens, verification performs B+1 target positions and emits a+1 tokens. Branching can increase a without increasing B, reducing target work per emitted token. Each unproductive position currently costs 210 body projections, 30 attention evaluations, and a full vocabulary projection. Shared tree prefixes are computed once. No neural drafter, additional vocabulary scan, or intermediate acceptance barrier is introduced.
proposal.source_evidence: candidate/inference.py:12 stores counts for every observed successor, but _draft at line 95 follows only preferred successors. _verify at line 128 computes all positions before decode checks acceptance at line 204. The checkpoint audit in experiments/0006/report.json records 30 layers and the tied [49152,576] head. The locked [KVCache implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/v0.32.0/mlx_lm/models/cache.py) supports offset trimming and overwriting speculative slots without shrinking allocation. [SuffixDecoding](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04975v3) supplies precedent for allocating speculation nodes using products of contextual successor frequencies. In-memory checks passed on 600 synthetic histories using the current index classes, 1,479 small-tree optimization cases, and 6,797 symbolic cache restorations; these are logical checks, not numerical or performance results.
proposal.generalization: Reducing full target computations per committed token is independent of hardware and backend and becomes valuable as target-model cost grows. The mechanism applies to decoder models with reversible causal caches and useful draft alternatives. This experiment uses only prompt tokens and committed outputs from the current request, with no training or cross-request reuse.
proposal.risk: Occurrence frequencies estimate acceptance imperfectly: wider trees may sacrifice useful depth. Tree construction, retained node KV tensors, and restoring the accepted branch add overhead. Cache aliasing, incorrect ancestor prefixes, or wrong RoPE offsets could break exactness. Native singleton shapes, layouts, rounding boundaries, and retained KV must match reference execution; symbolic checks do not establish BF16 parity.
proposal.history_relation: Extends round 0008’s accepted successor counts beyond its single-chain policy while retaining round 0006’s scalar arithmetic and weight-reuse schedule and round 0004’s fallback pipeline. Unlike round 0001, it introduces no batched numerical verification. Unlike rejected rounds 0009 and 0010, it preserves eager verification with one prediction materialization. No prior round tested branching within an unchanged target-position budget.

research.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Preserve model parameters, prefill computation, first-token selection, supported-model restrictions, and the scalar pipeline. Keep all state request-local. Prefill constructs only the existing prompt index; tree construction begins during decode at a drained boundary with cache offset C and pending token H[-1].

2. First obtain the existing linear draft and set B to its actual length, retaining all current context, capacity, and output-budget limits. For B<2, retain the existing path. Otherwise build a prefix tree from the same matched context. Assign root score 1 and child score equal to parent score times successor_count/sum(successor_counts). Repeatedly select the highest-scoring unselected child of any selected node until B draft nodes are selected. Extend the entire context without suffix backoff. Compare the sum of selected node scores with the linear chain’s score; use the tree only for a strict improvement, retaining the current chain on ties. Fix deterministic tie handling before evaluation. This score is a drafting heuristic, never an acceptance certificate.

3. Verify the pending root and B draft nodes using separate native singleton tensors. Preserve _project’s projection-major dependencies, all normalizations, residuals, SwiGLU operations, original full vocabulary heads, and argmax behavior. Compute each node once; do not run separate complete forwards for every root-to-leaf path or introduce tree-masked batched attention.

4. Within each layer, traverse nodes depth first, visiting stronger sibling branches last. Before inserting a node at depth d, trim the scratch cache to C+d; its remaining speculative entries must be exactly that node’s ancestors. Apply singleton RoPE at C+d, insert the node, and attend to exactly C+d+1 entries with the original helper and mask=None. Make each overwrite depend on completion of the preceding attention read. Preserve allocation capacity and native layouts. Save each node’s rotated K and original V separately for later restoration; do not clone the committed prefix for branches.

5. Materialize all predictions together once. Starting at the root, follow the unique child whose token equals the current node’s target argmax. Commit those child tokens and finally the prediction at the first node without a matching child. If a children were accepted, restore the cache path containing the root plus those a nodes: retain its common prefix with the final DFS path, trim the remainder, and append the saved KV tensors for the differing suffix. Do not use the linear trim(B-a) formula. End at offset C+1+a with the final emitted token pending and absent from KV. Submit restoration work during decode and ensure it is drained before return. Index committed tokens only.

6. Validate branching, repeated token labels under different parents, every acceptance depth, immediate rejection, leaf bonus tokens, ties, short budgets, capacity boundaries, scalar transitions, and request isolation. On independent target-model inputs, compare every node’s logits and KV against original singleton execution along its ancestor path, including subsequent greedy continuation after restoration. Confirm actual branches execute and investigate the first numerical discrepancy rather than relying only on matching immediate output IDs.

7. Record tree activations, verified node counts, accepted depths, and restoration writes without hot-path logging. Freeze the policy independently of benchmark prompts and results. Have the orchestrator run unchanged exact-token evaluation and both throughput confirmations against the current accepted candidate, retaining only an incremental gain of at least 1.03x in both runs.
research.reason: This offers a sound way to make the existing expensive verification budget produce more committed tokens. It preserves scalar numerical operations and avoids another serial acceptance barrier. Draft quality and cache-management overhead leave the net gain genuinely uncertain and worth testing.

proposal.name: Request-local tree speculation with scalar verification
proposal.idea: Allocate the current linear draft’s target-position budget to a tree selected from existing request-local successor counts. Verify each distinct node once with projection-major singleton operations, follow exact target predictions through the tree, and restore only the accepted path’s KV state.
proposal.cost_removed: A tree with B draft nodes performs B+1 target positions and emits a+1 tokens when a drafts are accepted. Better path coverage can reduce target positions per emitted token without increasing the per-verification node budget. Each avoided position removes 210 body projections, 30 attention evaluations, and one full vocabulary projection on this target. These are conditional savings: tree construction, retained KV tensors, restoration writes, and potentially shorter accepted paths add cost.
proposal.source_evidence: candidate/inference.py:12 stores alternative successor counts; :95 follows only preferred successors; :128–173 verifies all positions before acceptance. experiments/0006/report.json records the checkpoint audit, and round 0008 records the accepted drafting policy. harness/bench.py:20–29 times decode through a final synchronization. The pinned [Llama implementation](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/blob/v0.32.0/mlx_lm/models/llama.py) supplies the native singleton arithmetic; [KVCache](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm/v0.32.0/mlx_lm/models/cache.py) trims offsets without shrinking allocation. [SuffixDecoding](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.04975v3) supports occurrence-based tree scoring, but its cross-request state and published speedups are not adopted here.
proposal.generalization: Improving accepted tokens per fixed target-position budget is independent of hardware and backend. It can matter for large decoder models with useful continuation alternatives and reversible causal caches. Benefits remain conditional on acceptance and cache-management costs; this experiment does not establish frontier-scale throughput.
proposal.risk: Frequency scores are drafting heuristics, not target probabilities or acceptance certificates. Branching can sacrifice useful depth. Wrong ancestor prefixes, traversal-based RoPE positions, mutable KV snapshots, or incomplete restoration can break exactness. Retained tensors and cache-buffer copies may erase savings. Singleton shapes alone do not establish numerical parity.
proposal.history_relation: Extends round 0008’s counts while preserving round 0006’s scalar verification schedule and round 0004’s scalar pipeline. Round 0001’s block verifier failed exact evaluation without a numerical diagnosis; this proposal retains singleton operations. Rounds 0009 and 0010 tested additional acceptance barriers, whereas this experiment keeps eager verification and one joint prediction read. No prior round tested branching within the existing node budget.

review.plan:
1. Implement only inside candidate/. Preserve public interfaces, shared model parameters and module bindings, original prefill and first-token selection, supported-model restrictions, fixed-length generation after EOS, and zero/one-token budget behavior. Keep all state request-local. Prefill may build the existing prompt index; generated-token indexing, tree construction, verification, restoration, transfers, and completion work belong inside decode.

2. Enter speculation only after draining the scalar-output queue. Require history H, pending token H[-1], and every cache representing H[:-1] at common offset C. Obtain the unchanged linear draft first and set B to its actual length. Preserve its context, remaining-output, and allocated-capacity limits, including C+B+1 fitting every key/value allocation. Retain the current path for B<2. Also skip tree construction when every context queried along the linear draft has only one successor: its score cannot be improved under this budget. Preserve the existing scalar pipeline and recompute drafting decisions after every drain.

3. Build an ancestor-closed tree with exactly B nonroot nodes from the same matched context. Identify nodes by parent and token, with explicit stable IDs and depths; equal token labels under different parents remain distinct. Set root score to 1 and child score to parent_score times count(token)<redacted-path>(all successor counts). Extend the entire context without suffix backoff or index mutation. Maintain a frontier of unselected children of all selected nodes, including parents that already have selected children. Repeatedly select the highest score. Order equal-count children by stored preferred token first, then ascending token ID; resolve equal frontier scores by insertion order. Candidate storage may retain only the best B children per expanded context, but normalization must include all successors. Compare sums of nonroot scores using the same deterministic host arithmetic. Use the selected tree only for a strict computed improvement; retain the original chain on ties. Route any selected topology that is itself a chain through the existing linear verifier.

4. For an actual branching tree, choose one DFS preorder, visiting siblings in reverse child-priority order so stronger branches finish last. Preserve the mapping between node IDs, predictions, and saved KV. Verify the pending root and B draft nodes as separate native singleton tensors. Retain _project’s dependencies on consumed inputs and the original normalization, projection, residual, SwiGLU, full-head, and argmax operations. Compute each node once per layer. Preserve scalar shapes, layouts, dtypes, rounding boundaries, and inter-layer completion dependencies.

5. Within each layer, start from its committed prefix at C. Before processing a node at depth d, trim to C+d; DFS must leave exactly that node’s ancestors in the speculative slots. Apply singleton RoPE at C+d, insert the node, and attend to exactly C+d+1 entries with the original helper, scale, and mask=None. Gate both cache-buffer writes and consumed inputs on completion of the preceding attention read. Save the node’s rotated singleton K and singleton V before update_and_fetch; never retain the returned mutable prefix views as node snapshots. Use value-preserving independent snapshots if aliasing requires them. Preserve allocation capacity and native layout, and avoid cloning the committed prefix for branches.

6. Materialize all node predictions together once after complete verification. Starting at the root, follow only the current node’s child whose token equals that node’s target argmax. If a children are followed, emit their tokens and then the prediction at the first node without a matching child. Retain that node’s native prediction tensor as pending. This emits a+1 tokens, within the unchanged B+1 output allowance. Index committed tokens only. Exactness follows by induction along this path, conditional on each node matching original singleton execution under its ancestor prefix.

7. Let F be the final DFS cache path and P the accepted cache path, both including the pending root; P contains a+1 nodes. Compute their longest common prefix by node identity, of length l. For each layer, trim to C+l and append the saved singleton KV for P[l:] in order, without repeating projections or RoPE. End at C+a+1, with the final emitted token pending and absent from KV. Restoration may require writes even when the final DFS path is shorter than P; trim(B-a) is invalid. Preserve the committed prefix and allocation. Explicitly submit restoration arrays for evaluation, retain their dependencies through subsequent calls, and drain any remaining restoration before decode returns. A final synchronization must not be relied upon to execute an unsubmitted lazy graph. Avoid per-node or per-layer host barriers.

8. Validate tree selection against exhaustive small-tree cases and existing linear drafting. Exercise repeated token labels under different parents, deterministic ties, every acceptance depth, immediate rejection, leaf bonuses, acceptance on a nonfinal branch, final DFS paths shorter than accepted paths, capacity limits and subsequent scalar growth, short budgets, pipeline transitions, and request isolation. On independent target-model inputs, compare every node’s full logits and per-layer KV bitwise with original singleton calls teacher-forced along its ancestor path. Compare the complete restored valid cache prefix and subsequent greedy continuation. Confirm that branching and restoration actually execute. Investigate the first numerical discrepancy rather than accepting matching immediate token IDs as sufficient evidence.

9. Retain existing verification and acceptance counters; add branching activations, verified-node counts, and restored KV-slot counts without hot-path logging. Freeze the policy independently of benchmark prompts and results. Have the orchestrator run unchanged exact-token evaluation and both throughput confirmations against the current accepted candidate. Keep only an incremental gain of at least 1.03x in both confirmations. Record active-path status, correctness, work counts, and throughput separately; unavailable native execution is an implementation limitation, not an experiment result.
review.reason: No fundamental flaw was found. Independent in-memory checks passed 1,332 small-tree optimization cases and 4,670 acceptance/cache-restoration paths, using the current index classes across 320 synthetic histories. These establish logical checks only. The reviewed specification clarifies deterministic selection, node identity, cache dependencies, restoration, and complete decode accounting; native BF16 parity and net throughput remain for evaluation and benchmarking.

implementation.summary: Updated candidate/inference.py with budgeted tree selection, DFS singleton verification, accepted-path KV restoration, and counters. Local structural and NumPy stand-in checks passed. Native MLX numerical validation and benchmarking remain for the orchestrator; Metal is unavailable locally.
